item.title: A new Federal Reserve inquiry into the 2023 collapse of Silicon Valley Bank found that bank-supervision staff in the Biden era could have anticipated and prevented the bank’s failure
item.content:encoded: The report, commissioned by Trump ally Michelle Bowman, blamed bank-supervision staff in the Biden era.

item.title: Week Ahead for FX, Bonds: U.S. PMI Data, Various Central Bank Decisions in Focus
item.content:encoded: Provisional purchasing managers’ surveys measuring activity in the U.S. manufacturing and services sectors during September are due on Wednesday.

item.title: U.S. Leading Indicators Ticked Down in August
item.content:encoded: The Conference Board’s Leading Economic Index fell by 0.1% to 99.5 as consumer expectations remained a significant strain.

item.title: U.S. Industrial Production Unchanged in August
item.content:encoded: Production held flat last month after rising in July and June. Analysts polled by The Wall Street Journal expected a 0.3% increase.

item.title: Treasury Yields, Fed Rate-Hike Bets Rise After Strong U.S. Jobs Data
item.content:encoded: U.S. Treasury yields jump after significantly stronger-than-expected employment data for August lifted expectations of a Federal Reserve rate hike at the Sept. 16 meeting.

item.title: BOE Survey Points to Cooling Price Pressures
item.content:encoded: Businesses expect the prices they charge to rise by 3.8% over the coming 12 months, a decrease from the 3.9% expected in July.

item.title: Swiss Inflation Jumps on Higher Energy Prices
item.content:encoded: Swiss inflation jumped in August, reversing several months of cooling price growth as renewed tensions in the Middle East pushed global energy costs higher.

item.title: U.S. Housing Starts Fell in August
item.content:encoded: Housing starts fell 2.6% in August to 1.275 million. Economists expected a reading of 1.3 million and for starts to rise 4.9% over the month.

item.title: RBA Governor Bullock Says Inflation Fears Materializing
item.content:encoded: Bullock said inflation is likely to remain elevated for some time due to capacity pressures and the Middle East conflict.

item.title: The Bank of England kept its key interest rate unchanged, holding steady at a time when the Federal Reserve and European Central Bank have raised rates
item.content:encoded: The U.K. central bank is monitoring for signs that higher energy costs are spilling over into everyday prices.

item.title: AI juggernaut Anthropic’s IPO is coming later than expected, Trump pushed out major media outlets from the White House and Warren Buffett announced his retirement. Read more in today’s What’s News newsletter:
item.content:encoded: Plus, Howard Buffett steps into his father’s shoes and Trump bans certain news media from the White House.

item.title: U.K. Retail Sales Climbed Despite Inflation Pickup
item.content:encoded: Retail sales rebounded in August, helped by online sales, as consumers shrugged off recently rising inflation.

item.title: U.S. Treasury Yields Fall as Fed Regains Trust, BOE Leaves Rates Unchanged
item.content:encoded: Treasury yields declined from recent multiyear highs, reflecting increased trust in the Fed’s resolve to tame inflation.

item.title: A broad measure of American incomes reached a record high last year as upper-income households fared well and women’s pay gained ground compared with men
item.content:encoded: The annual Census report said upper-income households fared well and women’s pay gained ground compared with men.

item.title: Last month, the U.S. added an impressive 162,000 jobs and unemployment is low, but broad economic measures might be missing how much Americans’ costs have risen—and how many of them haven’t kept up
item.content:encoded: Official data shows steady growth and low unemployment but misses how rising costs have left many Americans behind.

item.title: A jittery Treasury market and the prospect of Fed rate increases risk making life more expensive for already cost-pressured Americans
item.content:encoded: A jittery Treasury market and the prospect of Fed rate increases risk making life more expensive for already cost-pressured Americans.

item.title: Consumer Sentiment Has Dropped in August, per Michigan Survey
item.content:encoded: Consumers’ economic mood is weaker this month versus July, according to preliminary results from the University of Michigan’s monthly survey.

item.title: Retail Sales Fell Last Month
item.content:encoded: Retailers’ sales fell by 0.6% last month to $763.6 billion, versus the 0.2% growth recorded in June.

item.title: The U.S. is pressuring Mexico to accept new rules for exports of AI hardware to prevent Chinese companies and other foreign firms from circumventing tariffs
item.content:encoded: Washington trade negotiators want to encourage more North American content in servers, chips and other equipment crossing America’s southern border.

item.title: Global Trading System Facing Fragmentation or Revamp At ‘Critical Juncture,’ WTO Says
item.content:encoded: The WTO said that economic activity would shrink significantly if world trade were to splinter into geopolitical blocs or regional groupings.
